# auto-work — instructions for AI assistants

If the user asks you to set up, configure, or run **auto-work**, read
[`docs/AI-SETUP.md`](./docs/AI-SETUP.md) and follow it.

Hard rules:

- **Do not start the loop** unless the user explicitly asks. Finish with
  `auto-work run --once --dry-run`, not `auto-work start`.
- **Do not commit secrets.** Agent keys go in the env file, never in config,
  prompts, or git.
- Ask only for the minimum. Detect the environment first with
  `auto-work detect`.
- **Keys first.** Import and validate keys with `auto-work keys import <file>`
  (or `init --keys-file <file>`) before asking for a project or platform. Ziki
  resolves both from the key. At least one `working` agent is required;
  manager/merger keys are optional.
- **No repo assumption.** The user may only have Ziki keys. Use
  `auto-work init --discover` (or `--github-repo`/`--fork-owner`) to find,
  fork and clone the repository; never invent one.
- **Run limits.** Every `start` has a limit (default 2 hours). Offer
  `--max-runtime`, `--max-cycles`, `--until`, `--max-deliveries`, or `--forever`.
- Prefer `auto-work init` and `auto-work config --validate` over hand-writing
  JSON. If you do write config, validate it.
- Full-auto flags (`--auto`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`,
  `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, `--yolo`) grant broad tool
  access. Explain that before choosing them.
- Never publish, push, or create GitHub resources for the user unless they
  explicitly ask for that action.
- **Branches:** commit and push only to `dev`. Never push or merge to `main`;
  `main` is release-only and is updated by a tested squash-merged PR from
  `dev`.

# auto-work An autonomous **Ziki** work loop for your repository. It watches the work feed, finds tickets, implements them in isolated worktrees, has the agent run your checks, opens pull requests, delivers them to Ziki, reviews other deliveries, and files evidence-backed ideas — continuously. It is provider-agnostic: use **opencode**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Gemini CLI**, or any custom command. It runs on **Linux, macOS, and Windows**. It queues **every** latest Ziki work kind: offers, review offers, claims, ready and open issues, test and acceptance reviews, idle and stranded work, merges and reconciliations, ideas, confirmations, closes, sense checks, importance marks, estimates, investigations, comments, stakes, PR and deployment reports, link repairs, releases, research jobs, bid votes and awards, and categorization. Unknown kinds and infrastructure blockers are surfaced in `status.health` instead of being silently dropped. Profile, auth, inbox, platform, provider and network failures are persisted, notified once, and retried with backoff. Capacity is adaptive, not rigid. Concurrency defaults to `"auto"` and follows the agents you configured; daily and per-cycle work caps default to `null` (no artificial cap). Only physical/provider and safety limits remain. `merge_fix` defaults to handoff: the loop reports PR state and never merges unless the profile sets `repo.mergeMode: "auto"`. Live status uses readable labels such as `#2624 typing-indicator` and `PR #1019 followup`. ## Requirements - Linux, macOS, Windows, or WSL. - Node.js **>= 20**, npm, git, and `gh` with `gh auth login` (`repo` scope). - The npm global bin directory (or `~/.local/bin`) on `PATH`; `doctor` warns if it is missing. - SSH or HTTPS push access to your fork. - A Ziki account with a project and a platform (`desktop`, `mobile`, `web`, …). - **At least one `working` agent key.** A `manager` or `merger` agent is optional; without one, merge reviews and manager-only actions are skipped. - A coding CLI (opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or a custom command) plus its provider auth. - The project toolchain your agent's checks need (for example Flutter/Dart, Node, Go, or Rust). - Network access and roughly 3 GB of free disk. - Project env values in `.env`/`.env.local` (or `executor.env`). - Optional: `notify-send` (Linux) / `osascript` (macOS) for desktop notifications. - Permission to push branches and open PRs on the target repository. - Optional: systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler for a managed service, Docker or a VM for isolation, and a scoped sudoers entry. - Windows: long paths enabled for deep repositories (`git config --system core.longpaths true`). Per-platform setup commands are in [`docs/requirements.md`](./docs/requirements.md). ## Let your AI set it up You only need your Ziki agent keys. Paste this into any AI assistant: ```text Read https://github.com/peter-abah/ziki-auto-work/blob/main/docs/AI-SETUP.md and set up ziki-auto-work for my Ziki project. I will provide agent keys. Do not assume a local repository: resolve the project and platform from Ziki, find (or fork and clone) the repository, write the config, then run `auto-work config --validate`, `auto-work doctor`, and `auto-work run --once --dry-run`. Do not start the loop. ``` The AI detects the environment, imports and validates your Ziki keys, resolves the project and platform from Ziki, finds or forks the repository, writes the config, and finishes with a dry run. It does **not** start the loop. ## Manual quickstart 1. **Create agents in Ziki** → Settings → Agents. Give at least one a `working` role. A `manager` or `merger` agent is optional; without one, the loop skips merge reviews, accept, cross-platform moves, and manager-only categorization. 2. **Create a keys file** in any editor (for example `keys.env`): ```text ZIKI_KEY1=... # working ZIKI_KEY2=... # manager (optional) ``` 3. **Install globally** (primary path for the long-running loop): ```bash npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work --install-links # The package creates a ~/.local/bin/auto-work shim when needed. # If you use --ignore-scripts, run: node /bin/auto-work.mjs install ``` `--install-links` avoids an npm 10 global-Git-install bug where npm can symlink to an incomplete cache directory. If your npm ignores the flag, use the archive instead: ```bash npm i -g https://github.com/peter-abah/ziki-auto-work/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz ``` The command above installs the **stable release on `main`**. To test the latest development build, install `#dev` instead: ```bash npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work#dev --install-links # archive alternative: npm i -g https://github.com/peter-abah/ziki-auto-work/archive/refs/heads/dev.tar.gz ``` 4. **Set it up from Ziki**: ```bash auto-work init --discover --keys-file keys.env ``` `init` validates every key, resolves the project and platform from Ziki, searches GitHub for the repository, detects the base branch, clones the repo, and detects the stack. It asks for the push target rather than silently choosing a personal fork. Use `--fork-owner ` + `--repo-url ` for a team fork, `--no-fork` for direct upstream pushes, or `--personal-fork` to make a personal fork explicit. 5. **Check and run**: ```bash auto-work doctor auto-work run --once --dry-run auto-work # sets up if needed, then runs in the foreground ``` The keys are stored in the config directory's `env` file with mode 600. They are never written to the config, prompts, or git. Project env values go in the clone's `.env`/`.env.local`; use `--env-file` to copy a prepared file. ### One-off with npx No global install needed: ```bash npx github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work init --keys-file keys.env npx github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work doctor npx github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work run --once --dry-run ``` `npx` builds the package from GitHub each time. For a loop that runs for days, install globally. ## What it does each cycle 1. Reads owner instructions, shared project notes, private agent notes and the mistake registry. 2. Merges the worker and manager work feeds. 3. Checks open escalations and the inbox; resumes answered tasks. 4. Handles owner requests from Ziki's agents bar. 5. Delivers tickets: confirm → bid → award → accept → heartbeat → worktree → implement → agent checks → commit → push → PR → Ziki delivery. 6. Reviews delivered PRs (test verdicts) and manager merge reviews. 7. Does auxiliary work: PR reports, bid votes, awards, comment upvotes, categorisation, idea triage, confirmations, estimates, investigations, importance marks, closes, sense checks, stakes, PR/deployment reports and link repairs. 8. Every few cycles, inspects the repo, configured context files, existing issues/ideas and recent work, then files evidence-backed ideas. A parity map is one optional context source, not a requirement. 9. Writes learnings to private agent notes and, when useful, shared notes. Work runs in parallel with adaptive capacity: deliveries, reviews, follow-ups and active claims follow the worker count; auxiliary work follows all keys; the agent ceiling follows the configured keys. Daily and per-cycle caps are off by default. State writes are serialized, so concurrent tasks do not lose updates. ## Run limits Runs have **no time limit by default**. You can impose one at start time; it is shown in `status` and there is no live-adjust command. ```bash auto-work start # no time limit auto-work start --max-runtime 4h auto-work start --max-cycles 20 auto-work start --until 2026-11-04T18:00:00Z auto-work start --max-deliveries 5 auto-work start --forever # no time/cycle/delivery limit auto-work start --all --max-runtime 90m auto-work start --verbose # stream structured logs ``` The loop finishes the current cycle, then stops with a reason (`max-runtime`, `max-cycles`, `until`, `max-deliveries`, `stop`, `network`, or `error`). `--once` still runs exactly one refresh and waits for the tasks it started. A foreground run shows one in-place status line; `--verbose` streams the structured log instead. ## Status, report and history ```bash auto-work status [--all] [--verbose] [--line] [--watch] auto-work report [--profile ] [--all] [--since 24h] [--json] auto-work history [--profile ] [--limit 50] ``` - `status` shows the run limit, elapsed and remaining time, stop reason, and in-flight counts. `--verbose` lists tasks with issue, status, PR, and last error. - `report` aggregates cycles, deliveries, reviews, discoveries, auxiliary work, failures, open escalations, issues/PRs touched, tokens and the stop reason. - `status --line` includes `tokens used/limit (percent)` when a token budget is configured. - `history` reads `history.jsonl` for claims, bids, awards, acceptances, deliveries, reviews, merge reviews, discoveries, auxiliary work, escalations, and failures. ## Profiles The config holds one or more **profiles**. Each profile is one project + repo + platform + agents + provider + checks + prompts. ```bash auto-work init --profile web auto-work profiles auto-work start --profile zedu-desktop auto-work start --all auto-work status --all ``` Per-profile state lives under `.../profiles//` (state, logs, worktrees, repo clone, results, `NEEDS-HUMAN.md`), so profiles do not interfere. ## Prompts per profile Each profile has its own prompt folder: ```text prompts//worker.md confirm.md triage.md review.md discovery.md owner.md pr.md ``` `auto-work init` copies the generic templates into your config directory and points the profile at them. Edit them freely. The engine passes project context (`{{projectName}}`, `{{stack}}`, `{{checks}}`, `{{issueUrl}}`, `{{worktree}}`, `{{memory}}`, `{{prContext}}`, …), so a prompt is data, not code. The worker writes the final PR body in `prBody`, following the target repo’s `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` when present. The orchestrator validates it minimally and falls back to a generated body if it is missing or unsafe. ## Models No model catalog is shipped. Models change too often. ```bash auto-work models --provider opencode # real IDs from `opencode models` auto-work models --provider claude # aliases + free text auto-work models --provider codex # reads ~/.codex/config.toml auto-work models --provider gemini # free text ``` `init` shows the available candidates and accepts a free-text model. Per-role models are supported, so triage/review can use a cheaper model while coding uses a stronger one: ```json "executor": { "provider": "claude", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5", "models": { "triage": "claude-haiku-4-5", "review": "claude-haiku-4-5" } } ``` `null` means “provider default”. ## Providers | Provider | Command | |---|---| | opencode | `opencode run --auto --format default --dir ` | | Claude Code | `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` | | Codex | `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C ` | | Gemini CLI | `gemini -p --yolo --skip-trust` | | custom | your command + `{{prompt}}` / `{{cwd}}` / `{{resultPath}}` / `{{model}}` | | registry | any headless CLI via `providers` in the config | | experimental | Aider, Goose, Copilot CLI, Cursor Agent, Qwen Code, Amp | `auto-work providers` lists built-ins, the experimental shortlist and custom providers. `auto-work providers --check` runs each version check. IDE-only tools need a CLI/headless mode; otherwise they are unsupported. See [`docs/providers.md`](./docs/providers.md) for auth, models, safe modes and cost notes. ## Human-in-the-loop (non-blocking) When the agent needs you it files a typed Ziki escalation (`question`, `work_authorization`, `blocker`, `scope_change`, `human_approval`). Ziki holds the details. The task goes `waiting_human`, the loop continues with other work, and resumes automatically when you answer. Auto-work also tells you directly: - the foreground status line always shows `Ziki needs you: N` - a desktop notification fires when the count goes from 0 to N, and again when it returns to 0 - no tokens or webhooks are needed; `hitl.notify` can be `auto`, `desktop`, `command`, or `off` - `NEEDS-HUMAN.md` mirrors the open items ```bash auto-work status --line # one line, tmux/script friendly auto-work status --watch # refresh every 30s auto-work escalations # detailed list; exits 1 when something is open auto-work approve # approve a config-repair proposal (loop applies it) auto-work reject # reject a config-repair proposal auto-work report # last run summary, including an abrupt end ``` ### Config repair (approval-gated self-healing) When a health blocker has an enabled repair strategy (see `repair` in Configuration), a `config-doctor` agent diagnoses the failure and proposes a minimal config patch. The orchestrator validates it against `repair.mutablePaths` — protected paths (repo/executor/providers/agents, hitl/repair, prompts, secrets) are refused even if listed — and posts it as a `human_approval` escalation on Ziki. Reply starting with `APPROVE` to apply it (atomic save + timestamped backup, hot-reload, loop resumes); anything else keeps the escalation open and triggers a revised proposal (max rounds configurable, then expiry). No agent output is ever applied without your approval. If Ziki is unreachable, use the local fallback above; the loop picks the decision up on its next repair pass. If you run headless, use `auto-work status --line` or configure `hitl.notify: "command"` with a local script. ## Run summary When a run ends — limit reached, `stop`, SIGINT/SIGTERM, or a crash — auto-work prints a short summary: duration, stop reason, cycles, deliveries, reviews, discoveries, aux, failures, interrupted tasks, and `Ziki needs you: N`. It writes `LAST-RUN.json` and `LAST-RUN.md` to the profile state directory. If the process was killed abruptly, the next start (or `auto-work report`) shows the last saved state and marks the run incomplete. Token usage is reported where the provider exposes it, with optional regex or estimated fallback. `limits.maxTokensPerRun` and `tokenWarnPercent` warn and stop after the current task (`stopReason: "token-limit"`). A hard provider quota stops with `provider-limit`; rate limits back off and retry. ## Checks and safety - `checks[]` is project guidance for the agent. The worker runs the commands, captures evidence, and reports results in the PR/Ziki delivery. The orchestrator does **not** run checks and never blocks delivery on repo state. - Ziki peer review and the repository's CI are the quality gates. - Workflow rules come from `workflow`: max files, max lines, branch prefix, commit types. One ticket per branch/PR. - Protected files, max files/lines and secrets are rejected before commit. - Daily caps, `maxActiveClaims`, `pause`/`resume`, and a `STOP` kill switch. - State writes are serialized; in-flight work is tracked so duplicate picks do not start. - On restart, stale agent PIDs are killed and stale worktrees are cleaned up. PRs that already exist are reconciled instead of re-running the worker. - `stop` aborts in-flight tasks and kills child process trees, including grandchildren on timeout. - GitHub/git network failures retry with backoff; tasks that crash while pushing/opening a PR are requeued instead of left `working`. - The loop **never merges**. A manager/merger agent does that on GitHub. - Project env comes from `.env`/`.env.local` copied into each worktree, plus `executor.env`. `doctor` validates `repo.requiredEnv`. ## PR tracking and follow-up After delivery, auto-work can track its own PRs through `profile.prTracking`: - poll delivered PRs for state, checks, mergeability, reviews and comments; - read GitHub review comments and failed check logs; - run a bounded follow-up worker on the same branch for actionable feedback; - push to the same PR, update its body, and report status back to Ziki; - mark the task `done` when merged or `skipped` when closed; - escalate only when attempts are exhausted, a product decision is needed, or access/policy blocks progress. It still does not merge. Ziki’s peer/manager gate and GitHub’s branch protection are separate and external. Full-auto flags (`--auto`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, `--yolo`) grant broad tool access. Read [`docs/safety.md`](./docs/safety.md) before running unattended. ## Commands ```bash auto-work install [--keys-file ] [--service] [--profile ] auto-work # set up if needed, then run in the foreground auto-work init [--keys-file ] [--profile ] [--example ] [--from-file ] [--yes] [--discover] [--fork] [--fork-owner ] [--repo-url ] [--personal-fork] [--no-fork] [--dry-run] [--env-file ] auto-work keys import auto-work keys check auto-work uninstall [--dry-run] [--keep-data] [--yes] auto-work detect [--json] auto-work models [--provider

] [--profile ] [--json] auto-work providers [--check] auto-work profiles auto-work doctor [--profile ] [--json] auto-work start [--profile ] [--foreground] [--verbose] [--once] [--dry-run] [--all] [--max-runtime 2h] [--max-cycles N] [--until ISO] [--max-deliveries N] [--forever] auto-work run [--profile ] [--verbose] [--once] [--dry-run] auto-work stop | pause | resume auto-work status [--all] [--verbose] [--line] [--watch] auto-work report [--profile ] [--all] [--since 24h] [--json] auto-work history [--profile ] [--limit 50] auto-work logs [--profile ] [--lines 80] [--follow] auto-work escalations | memory | prompts auto-work approve | reject auto-work config [--show] [--validate] ``` ## Configuration - Config: platform config dir + `auto-work/config.json` - Secrets: same dir + `env` (mode 600) - State: platform state dir + `auto-work/profiles//` See [`docs/config.md`](./docs/config.md) for the full schema. ## Windows Use PowerShell. Paths resolve to `%APPDATA%\auto-work` (config and keys) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\auto-work` (state, cache and the command shim). There is no `chmod`; the installer writes the shim for you. For example: ```powershell npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work --install-links # If the npm bin dir is not on PATH, add %APPDATA%\npm and/or # %LOCALAPPDATA%\auto-work\bin to your user PATH. auto-work init --keys-file .\keys.env auto-work doctor auto-work run --once --dry-run ``` `install.ps1` is included in the package for clone/local installs. The service command uses Task Scheduler when available and falls back to a detached process. Run an elevated terminal only if you explicitly need it. ## Uninstall ```bash auto-work uninstall --dry-run # show what would be removed auto-work uninstall # confirm, then remove auto-work uninstall --keep-data # remove the service and shim, keep config/state auto-work uninstall --yes # skip the confirmation ``` It removes the systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler entry, the command shim, the config directory (config, keys, prompts), the state directory (profiles, logs, worktrees, repo clones, results), the cache, and the known legacy `~/.local/share/auto-work` / `~/.local/state/auto-work` paths. Then run: ```bash npm uninstall -g ziki-auto-work ``` ## Branches - **`main`** — stable release and the repository default branch. Plain installs get this. - **`dev`** — active development. All commits are pushed here. Never commit directly to `main`. When `dev` is tested, open a PR `dev` → `main` and squash-merge it. `main` then becomes the new release. ```bash git switch dev ``` ## Development ```bash npm ci npm run check npm test npm run build npm run verify # build + fail if dist/ is stale ``` Node 20+. TypeScript is dev-only; the runtime dependency is `cross-spawn` for reliable Windows process launching. `dist/` is committed so `npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work --install-links` works without devDependencies. After changing `src/`, run `npm run build` and commit the updated `dist/`; CI fails if `dist/` is stale. ## License MIT. See [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE).

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Added an adaptive Ziki API layer. Validation failures now strip unknown or
  rejected fields, repair oversized values, cache the learned contract per
  endpoint, and retry. Full Ziki error details are logged instead of the opaque
  `Invalid input.` message.
- If deterministic repair cannot fix a `400`/`422`, an `apiRepair` agent gets
  the operation, attempted payload and error body, and may return a corrected
  payload or abandon the action with a reason.
- Discovery now uses the live minimal create-idea payload (no unsupported
  `platform` field) and sanitizes idea summaries to plain 20–300 character text.
- Added tests for contract keys, unknown-field stripping, truncation, repair
  callbacks, the minimal idea payload, and summary sanitization.

- Failed work now releases its Ziki claim before being requeued or marked failed.
  Previously a retryable failure (notably “agent made no changes”) kept the
  claim, counted against `maxActiveClaims`, and could leave the loop idle with
  no dispatchable work.
- PR follow-up stops and marks the task skipped when Ziki returns `404` for the
  issue, instead of retrying `Issue not found` forever.
- Discovery now uses the current run’s cycle count in both the dispatcher and
  `discoveryPass`, so its cadence works correctly after a restart.
- Removed the daily delivery/review/discovery caps and the per-cycle auxiliary
  cap from the config schema and dispatcher. There are no daily work caps.
- Runs have no time limit by default; `--max-runtime`/`maxRuntimeMinutes` are
  still available when a limit is wanted.
- `maxAttemptsPerTask` and `maxOpenEscalations` now accept `null` for unlimited
  and default to `null`; the init template and examples no longer reintroduce
  the old caps.
- Removed the daily delivery/review/discovery caps and the per-cycle auxiliary
  cap from the config schema and dispatcher. There are no daily work caps.

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue with exploit details. Report privately through
GitHub Security Advisories on the repository, or contact the maintainer.

Include the version, platform, a minimal reproduction, and the impact.

## Supported versions

This is development-stage software with no versioned releases. Security fixes
land on `main`.

## Scope and expectations

auto-work runs a coding agent with broad tool access when
`permissionMode: "auto"`. This is documented in [`docs/safety.md`](./docs/safety.md).
Reports that only demonstrate “the agent can run commands” are expected
behaviour, not vulnerabilities.

In scope:

- secret leakage in config, logs, prompts, or PR bodies;
- path traversal or command injection in the orchestrator;
- authentication/authorization bugs in the Ziki client;
- unsafe default file permissions;
- supply-chain issues in dependencies.

Out of scope:

- the coding CLI itself (report to its maintainer);
- Ziki server-side bugs (report to Ziki);
- damage caused by deliberately running full-auto mode without isolation.

# AI setup guide

You are setting up **auto-work** for a user. Follow this checklist exactly.

## Requirements checklist

Confirm these before installing. Missing items are reported by `auto-work doctor`.

- Linux, macOS, Windows, or WSL.
- Node.js >= 20, npm, git, and `gh` with `gh auth login` (`repo` scope).
- SSH or HTTPS push access to the fork.
- A Ziki account with a project and platform.
- **At least one `working` agent key.** `manager`/`merger` is optional.
- A coding CLI (opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or custom) and its
  provider auth.
- The project toolchain used by checks.
- Network access, ~3 GB free disk, and push/PR permission.
- Optional: systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler, Docker/VM, sudoers.

Per-platform commands are in [`requirements.md`](./requirements.md).

## Hard rules

- **Do not start the loop.** Finish with `auto-work run --once --dry-run`, not
  `auto-work start`.
- **Do not commit secrets.** Ziki keys go in the env file, never in config,
  prompts, or git.
- Ask only for what you cannot detect.
- If the user wants full-auto flags, explain the risk first.
- Keys come first. Do not ask for a project ID or platform before you have a
  valid key.
- Do not assume a local repository. The user may only have Ziki keys; discover
  or fork the repo.

## 1. Install and detect

```bash
npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work --install-links
auto-work detect --json
```

`--install-links` avoids an npm 10 global-Git-install bug. If it is ignored,
install the archive instead:
`npm i -g https://github.com/peter-abah/ziki-auto-work/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz`.

If the user prefers a one-off, replace `auto-work` with
`npx github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work`.

This installs the stable `main` release. For development builds, use
`github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work#dev` or
`npx github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work#dev`. Do not install `#dev` for a normal
user unless they explicitly want to test unreleased work.

This reports the OS, Node version, stack files, installed coding CLIs, the
config path and the active profile.

## 2. Get the keys

Tell the user to create agents in **Ziki → Settings → Agents**. They need at
least one `working` agent. A `manager` or `merger` agent is optional: without
one, merge reviews, accept, cross-platform moves, and manager-only
categorization are skipped. Awards, confirmations, and idea verdicts still work
at weight 1.

Ask them to save the keys in a file:

```text
ZIKI_KEY1=...
ZIKI_KEY2=...
```

Then import and validate:

```bash
auto-work keys import keys.env
```

`keys import` writes the keys to the env file (mode 600) and checks each one
with `GET /api/v1/agents/me`. It prints a table of env name, agent, level and
project, and assigns `working` → workers and `manager`/`merger` → managers.
Warn if there is no manager key; leave `managers` empty instead of inventing
one.

If the user prefers to do it in one command:

```bash
auto-work init --keys-file keys.env
```

`init` runs the same import and validation before it asks anything else.

If the user has no keys, print the instructions above and stop. Do not ask for a
project or platform first.

## 3. Resolve the project and platform from Ziki

The validated key already belongs to a project. `init` reads `project_id`,
`project_slug` and `projects` from `GET /api/v1/agents/me`, and reads the real
platform slugs from `GET /api/v1/platforms` (usually `desktop`, `mobile`,
`web`). Prefer the platform that matches the repository; never use the stack as
the platform.

If the key lists several projects, show them and let the user pick. The default
is the key's own project.

## 4. Discover the repository

The user may not have a clone or fork. Do not assume one exists.

```bash
auto-work init --discover --keys-file keys.env
auto-work init --discover --keys-file keys.env --dry-run
```

`--discover`:

1. Resolves the project and platform from the keys.
2. Searches GitHub for the repository using the project slug and platform
   (`zedu` + `desktop` → `zeduchat/zedu-desktop`).
3. Shows candidates and asks once if ambiguous.
4. Uses an existing fork, or asks before creating one. Non-interactive runs
   need `--fork`.
5. Detects the default branch, prefers `staging` as the base if it exists, and
   clones the fork.
6. Detects the stack from the clone and selects the checks preset.
7. Writes the config and copies the prompts.

Useful overrides: `--project-slug`, `--platform`, `--github-repo`,
`--upstream`, `--repo-url`, `--fork-owner`, `--base`, `--default-branch`,
`--stack`, `--checks`, `--profile`, `--team-lead`, `--env-file`,
`--discovery` / `--no-discovery`, `--context-file <paths>`, and
`--discovery-focus <text>`.

Discovery is not parity. It inspects the repo, optional context files, existing
Ziki issues/ideas and recent work, then files ideas. Use `--context-file` for
project docs/specs (for example an OpenAPI file or architecture doc) and
`--discovery-focus` for a plain-language brief. A `--parity` file is only an
optional context document for web-vs-desktop parity profiles.

If discovery cannot resolve the repo, ask for the upstream `owner/name` and
whether the user wants a fork. Never invent a repository.

Stack presets:

- `pubspec.yaml` → Flutter → `flutter`
- `package.json` → Node → `node`
- `pyproject.toml` → Python → `python`
- `go.mod` → Go → `go`
- `Cargo.toml` → Rust → `rust`

## 4b. Environment values

Project env belongs in the clone:

- `auto-work init --discover` copies `.env.example` to `.env` if needed.
- Ask the user to fill `.env`/`.env.local`, or pass `--env-file <path>` to copy
  a prepared file (mode 600).
- Never put secrets in the config, prompts, or git.
- `doctor` checks `repo.requiredEnv` keys exist without printing values.

Provider auth (opencode/Claude/Codex/Gemini) is separate: each CLI uses its own
login. `executor.env` can pass extra variables to the agent and checks.

## 5. Write the config

Preferred: create a JSON file and apply it.

```bash
auto-work init --from-file setup.json
auto-work config --validate
```

Or use the interactive wizard:

```bash
auto-work init --keys-file keys.env
```

The config is version 3 and has `profiles` + `activeProfile`:

```json
{
  "version": 3,
  "activeProfile": "my-project",
  "profiles": {
    "my-project": {
      "ziki": { "baseUrl": "https://ziki.dev", "projectId": "project_...", "projectSlug": "my-project", "platform": "web" },
      "stack": "Next.js + TypeScript",
      "repo": { "url": "...", "upstream": "...", "base": "main", "githubRepo": "owner/repo", "forkOwner": "me", "defaultBranch": "main" },
      "agents": { "workers": ["ZIKI_KEY2"], "managers": ["ZIKI_KEY1"] },
      "executor": { "provider": "opencode", "model": null },
      "checks": [],
      "prompts": { "dir": "prompts/my-project" },
      "pr": { "templateFile": "prompts/my-project/pr.md" }
    }
  }
}
```

The config is written to the platform config directory:

- Linux: `~/.config/auto-work/config.json`
- macOS: `~/Library/Preferences/auto-work/config.json`
- Windows: `%APPDATA%\auto-work\config.json`

See [`config.md`](./config.md) for the full schema.

## 6. Prompts

`auto-work init` copies the generic prompts into the config directory and sets
`prompts.dir` to that folder. If you are writing the config by hand, copy them:

```bash
auto-work prompts --profile <profile>
```

Then edit `prompts/<profile>/worker.md`, `review.md`, `confirm.md`, `triage.md`,
`discovery.md`, `owner.md`, and `pr.md` for the project. The engine fills
`{{projectName}}`, `{{stack}}`, `{{checks}}`, `{{issueUrl}}`, `{{worktree}}`,
`{{memory}}`, `{{previousError}}`, and other placeholders.

## 7. Validate and dry-run

```bash
auto-work config --validate
auto-work doctor
auto-work doctor --json
auto-work run --once --dry-run
```

`doctor` prints the key table, checks the selected provider, `gh`
auth/scopes, repository push permission, the Ziki project/platform, the repo
clone, the base branch, fork access, disk space, env files and
`repo.requiredEnv`, desktop notifications, and stale lock/PID/worktree state.
`--json` is available for automation. The dry run builds the queue and performs
**no Ziki or GitHub writes**.

## 8. Report back

Tell the user:

- the config path and active profile,
- the key table (env name, agent, level, project),
- the provider and resolved models,
- the checks that will run,
- the number of items in the dry-run queue,
- the run limit (none by default) and flags: `--max-runtime`, `--max-cycles`,
  `--until`, `--max-deliveries`, `--forever`,
- how they will be notified (desktop notification + `status --line`),
- that the loop is **not running**,
- the command to start it: `auto-work` (or `auto-work start`).

- **opencode**: `opencode models` lists real IDs. `--auto` is used for headless

- **Claude Code**: `--model` accepts aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) or full

Use the packaged `install.ps1` or
`npm i -g github:peter-abah/ziki-auto-work --install-links`. Paths resolve to

- `doctor` FAIL lines are the source of truth.
- `auto-work keys check` fixes key problems (invalid, revoked, wrong level).
- `gh auth status` fixes GitHub access.
- `ssh-add` fixes fork access.
- `auto-work config --validate` fixes config shape.
- `auto-work models` fixes model names.

## The cycle

1. `poll` — read open escalations and the inbox; resume answered tasks.
2. `memory` — refresh instructions, shared notes, private notes, mistakes.
3. `feed` — merge worker and manager work feeds with ETags.
4. `platform` — refresh the platform's issues and ideas (10 min cache).
5. `queue` — filter to this profile's platform, prioritise, skip recent/blocked.
6. `heartbeat` — keep active claims alive.
7. `owner` — handle one owner request.
8. `dispatch` — start work in parallel: deliveries, reviews, auxiliary tasks
   and discovery, subject to per-kind limits and `maxConcurrentAgents`.
   `inFlightKeys` prevents duplicate picks.
9. `delivery` — confirm/bid/award/accept, implement, agent checks, push, PR,
   deliver.
10. `follow-up` — observe delivered PRs, address review comments and failing
    checks on the same branch, and push to the same PR.
11. `review` — test verdicts and manager merge reviews. Review preflight
    skips merged/closed PRs, failing or pending checks, merge conflicts, and
    issues that already have enough good-to-merge verdicts.
12. `aux` — PR reports/deployments, bid votes, awards, comment upvotes,
    categorisation, idea triage, confirmations. Auxiliary kinds rotate by kind
    so one large queue cannot starve the others.
13. `discovery` — every N cycles, file evidence-backed ideas. When due, it
    reserves an agent slot before auxiliary dispatch so it cannot be crowded
    out by a full pool.
14. `cleanup` — remove old worktrees.
15. save state, then sleep or wait for an in-flight task.

## API adaptation and self-correction

Ziki is a remote API, so its live schema is treated as a runtime capability, not
a compile-time contract. Every write goes through the adaptive request layer:

- known-rejected fields are cached per endpoint and stripped before sending;
- unknown validation fields are removed from the body and retried;
- oversized strings/arrays are repaired when the API reports a maximum;
- full validation details are included in errors and logs;
- if deterministic repair cannot fix a `400`/`422`, a short-lived `apiRepair`
  agent receives the operation, attempted payload and full error body and may
  return a corrected payload or abandon it with a reason;
- abandoned actions are recorded instead of silently discarded.

The learned contract is stored in `state.apiContracts` so the same field is not
sent again on the next run. Discovery also sanitizes idea summaries before
sending them.

## Roles

A profile needs at least one working agent. Managers/mergers are optional; when
absent, merge reviews and manager-only actions are skipped, awards fall back to a
worker (self-award), and confirmations/idea verdicts run at weight 1. If no
worker exists, manager keys perform working tasks.

## Run limits and concurrency

The loop polls every worker and manager feed, binds offers/claims/reviews to the
agent that owns them, reserves one task per key, heartbeats delivered and
queued claims, and releases undelivered claims on provider quota, context
overflow, permanent failure and shutdown. The Ziki project's `maxActiveClaims`
(2 for `zedu`) is read at startup and used as the hard claim ceiling.

`maxRuntimeMinutes` (no limit by default), `maxCycles`, `stopAt`,
`maxDeliveriesTotal`, or an explicit stop ends the loop after the current
cycle. `maxCycles` is counted from the start of the current run; the status and
report show both the run cycle count and the lifetime total. Limits are chosen at `start` and recorded in `status.json` with elapsed
and remaining time and a stop reason. Concurrency defaults to 2 deliveries,
1 review, 2 auxiliary tasks, 1 discovery, and 4 agents total; delivery
concurrency is also capped by `maxActiveClaims`.

## Discovery and rules

`init --discover` resolves the project/platform from the keys, searches GitHub
for the repository, uses or creates a fork, detects branches, clones, and
detects the stack. Workflow rules live in `profile.workflow`; prompts receive
the resolved rules, protected files, PR target/head, team lead and PR template
via placeholders, and the orchestrator enforces file/line limits.

## Env

Worktrees receive the configured `repo.envFiles` (`.env`, `.env.local` by
default). Agents inherit the process env, then `executor.env`, then provider
and per-run env. Toolchain
directories are prepended to `PATH`. Env/auth/tool failures are classified as
blockers instead of silent retries.

## Notifications and run summary

Open escalations are summarized as `needsYou` in `status.json`. The status line
shows `Ziki needs you: N`; desktop notifications fire on count changes. Each
run builds a `RunSummary`, updated on every save, written to `LAST-RUN.json` /
`LAST-RUN.md` and printed on clean exit. Unclean runs are detected on the next
start or by `auto-work report`.

## State and history

All `state.json` and `status.json` writes go through a mutex, so concurrent
tasks do not lose updates. `history.jsonl` records claim/bid/award/accept,
delivery, review, merge review, discovery, auxiliary work, escalation, failure
and stop entries for `auto-work report` and `auto-work history`. Agent PIDs are
recorded so a restart can kill stale children; existing PRs are reconciled
instead of re-running the worker.

## Result contract

Every agent run writes a JSON result to an absolute path. The orchestrator
reads it and decides what to do. The contract is provider-independent.

## State

Each profile has its own state directory. `state.json` holds tasks, escalations,
counters and feed ETags. `status.json` is the human-readable
snapshot. Locks are per profile, so `start --all` can run multiple profiles.

## Worktrees

The harness clones the fork into `profiles/<profile>/repos/repo`, fetches `upstream`,
and creates a worktree per ticket and per review. `.env` is copied from the
clone so builds work. Worktrees are removed after delivery/review failures and
cleaned up after tasks finish.

## HITL

Ziki escalations are stored in state with the asking agent's name. The poll pass
uses that agent's key to read the answer. A `waiting_human` task is not picked
again until it is answered.

## Checks

Checks are agent-owned. `checks[]` is rendered into the worker prompt through
`{{checks}}`; the agent runs the commands and reports evidence in the result and
PR. The orchestrator does not run checks, does not baseline failures, and does
not gate delivery on repository state. Ziki peer review and CI are the quality
gates. The only orchestrator gates are protected files, max files/lines, and
secrets.

## Ziki drift

Ziki changes. Work-feed kinds, statuses, platforms, routes, payloads, auth, rate
limits and UI paths are assumptions in `ziki.ts`, `types.ts`, `queue.ts`,
`orchestrator.ts`, prompts and fixtures. Re-check them against the live Ziki
API/UI periodically, then update code, docs, tests and examples together.

# Configuration reference

The config is a **workspace** with one or more **profiles** (config version 4;
v3 configs migrate with `auto-work migrate`).

## v4 — zero runtime defaults

Every behavioral value lives in the profile. The runtime never substitutes a
built-in: a missing key fails loud (`config:missing_key` blocker → repair
proposal → `NEEDS-HUMAN.md`).

- `config/init-templates.json` is the only place defaults exist (versioned
  snapshot of last-known-good values, not truth). `init`/`init --discover`
  writes them explicitly into `config.json`; `migrate` fills v3 configs the
  same way (backup `.v3.bak`).
- `auto-work migrate [--dry-run]` — v3 → v4, reports filled sections.
- `auto-work config --explain` — per-section provenance: `explicit` (you
  wrote it), `template` (would fill from init templates), `missing`.
- v4 requires every section listed in `validateV4Required` (transport,
  operations, queue, reviewGate, heartbeatPolicy, decisions, noop, votes,
  idea, apiRepair, capacity, urls, discover, github, safety, checksDefaults,
  outbox, bootstrap, offline, loop, pr, repo, discovery, timing, statuses,
  health, limits, workflow, prTracking, ziki.endpoints, …). See
  [`CONFIG-REGISTRY.md`](./CONFIG-REGISTRY.md) for the literal → section map.

## Operations and transport (P2a)

`ZikiClient` has four primitives: `route()` (endpoint templates only, throws
`unknown endpoint` with no built-in fallback), `request()`, `invoke(group,
name)` (method/expect/timeout/retries from `operations.<group>.<name>`), and
`listAllOp()` (cursor pagination from `operations.<group>.<name>.pagination`,
all keys required). The ~80 thin wrappers (`bid()`, `heartbeat()`, …) carry
only field data; HTTP method, expected shape, pagination and transport
(auth scheme, user agent, timeouts, backoff caps) are config. `route` in an
operation maps to a different endpoint name when they differ
(e.g. `withdrawBid` → `bid`).

## Policy tables (P2b)

Queue buckets/priorities, status vocabulary, review gate, heartbeat,
decisions, noop patterns, votes, idea shaping, API repair, capacity, URLs —
all required config with fail-loud readers. Unknown Ziki kinds sort after
every known kind into the `other` bucket and raise a visible
`unknown_vocabulary`/`unknown_kind` warning instead of dropping work.

## External surfaces (P2c)

Discovery scoring/suffixes/timeouts/stacks/check presets, GitHub state and
merge maps, check defaults, secret/protected patterns, outbox, offline —
all config. Local tooling (provider CLIs, gh plumbing, doctor env checks)
stays code; see CONFIG-REGISTRY §E.

## Self-healing (P3)

Only hard failures park without repair: provider/model errors and missing
keys (`config:missing_key` never fires for those — there is nothing to
propose). Everything else gets a deterministic diagnosis first (template
backfill for missing keys and unknown endpoints, aux-bucket placement for
unknown kinds, `statuses.known` appends for drift vocabulary), then a
`config-doctor` agent proposal, then a Ziki `human_approval` escalation
(`APPROVE` applies; anything else re-proposes, bounded by `maxRounds`).
New strategies: `config:missing_key`, `config:unknown_endpoint`,
`*:unknown_kind`, `*:unknown_vocabulary`. New kind names are creatable under
`queue.priorities.*` (numbers only); new endpoint names are never invented.

No deterministic bypasses: every non-hard failure (anything except
provider/model errors and missing keys) reaches the config-doctor agent —
there is no code path that concludes "unfixable" on its own. The doctor may
fetch unauthenticated public URLs (GET only) to investigate moved routes;
the orchestrator live-verifies proposed endpoint ops (only a proven 404 +
"no such API route" drops an op) before escalation. The human APPROVE gate
is the only stop.

- `projectId`, `projectSlug`: the project the agent keys belong to.
- `platform`: the Ziki platform slug used to filter issues and ideas. Get the
  real values from `GET /api/v1/platforms` (`desktop`, `mobile`, `web`, …).
- `projectName`: human name used in prompts.
- `platformCategoryId`: optional platform id, for discovery.

`stack` is separate from `platform`: it is the technology label used in prompts
and check presets (`Flutter`, `Next.js`, …).

## repo

- `url`: your fork clone (push target).
- `upstream`: canonical repo (fetch/base).
- `base`: branch PRs target.
- `githubRepo`: `owner/name` for `gh`.
- `forkOwner`: fork org/user for `gh pr create --head`.
- `pushMode`: `personal-fork`, `team-fork`, or `upstream`. `upstream` pushes
  directly to the canonical repo and uses `forkOwner` = upstream owner.
- `defaultBranch`: used to check whether a merge is in the default branch.
- `teamLead`: PR template handle.
- `protectedFiles`: glob patterns; matched against changed paths and basenames.
- `envFiles`: files copied from the clone into every ticket/review worktree
  (default `[".env", ".env.local"]`). They stay protected and are never committed.
- `requiredEnv`: env keys `doctor` requires in those files; values are never printed.

## agents

Env var names, not keys. Example: `workers: ["ZIKI_KEY2"]`,
`managers: ["ZIKI_KEY1"]`. `init` assigns `working` keys to workers and
`manager`/`merger` keys to managers. The env file lives next to the config and is
mode 600.

`managers` may be empty. Without a manager/merger, the loop skips merge
reviews, accept, cross-platform moves, and manager-only categorization.
Working keys still bid, award (self-award), confirm at weight 1, triage ideas,
and deliver. If `workers` is empty, manager keys are used for working tasks.

## executor

- `provider`: `opencode`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `custom`, an experimental shortlist id, or a key in `providers`.
- `model`: default model, or `null` for provider default.
- `models`: per-role overrides (`worker`, `review`, `triage`, `confirm`,
  `discovery`, `owner`).
- `timeoutMs`: per-agent timeout.
- `permissionMode`: `auto` (bypass flags) or `safe` (least-privilege; may block).
- `extraArgs`: provider-specific flags.
- `env`: extra environment variables.
- `usage`: optional token parsing (`regex` and/or `estimate`).
- `command`, `args`, `promptMode`: custom provider only.

## checks

`checks[]` is guidance for the agent, not an orchestrator gate. The worker runs
the commands and reports the evidence; the orchestrator does not execute them
and does not block delivery on repository state.

- `name`: label shown to the agent.
- `command`: executable or a key from `toolchain`.
- `args`: arguments.
- `filesOnly`, `include`, `reporter`, `baseline`, `timeoutMs`, `required`,
  `env`: accepted for backward compatibility but ignored by the orchestrator.

The agent receives the resolved command lines through the `{{checks}}` prompt
placeholder. Ziki peer review and CI remain the quality gates.

## prompts and pr

`prompts.dir` is the per-profile prompt folder. The worker writes the final PR
body in `prBody`, using the target repo’s template when present; `pr.templateFile`
is only a fallback. Both paths are relative to the package root or absolute.
The engine fills placeholders such as `{{projectName}}`, `{{stack}}`,
`{{checks}}`, `{{issueUrl}}`, `{{worktree}}`, `{{memory}}`,
`{{previousError}}`, `{{issueContext}}`, `{{prContext}}`, `{{ticket}}`,
`{{teamLead}}`.

## prTracking

- `enabled`: track delivered PRs and follow up on feedback.
- `pollMinutes`: how often to check each PR.
- `maxFollowUps`: maximum follow-up pushes per PR before escalation.
- `fixFailingChecks`: let the follow-up worker address failing checks.
- `fixReviewComments`: let it address review comments/changes requested.

Follow-up uses the existing branch/worktree, pushes to the same PR, and never
opens a second PR. It does not merge; Ziki and GitHub merge gates remain
external.

## platformMatch

Keywords or a regex. Used to decide whether a work item belongs to this profile.
Issues already tagged with the platform are included regardless.

## discovery

Work discovery is a periodic ideation pass: the agent reads the repository,
configured context files, existing Ziki issues/ideas and recent work, then files
evidence-backed ideas. It does not claim, fix or review anything itself.

- `enabled`: turn the pass on or off. New `init` profiles enable it by default;
  `--no-discovery` disables it. It is no longer tied to `parityFile`.
- `contextFiles`: optional list of docs/specs to read. Relative paths are tried
  in the repo worktree, then the package root; absolute paths are used as-is.
  Backend examples: `openapi.yaml`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
  `docs/DATABASE.md`.
- `focus`: optional plain-language brief for what discovery should look for.
- `parityFile`: optional, backward-compatible. It is just one context file,
  useful for web-vs-desktop parity profiles. It is **not** required for
  discovery.
- `maxIdeasPerRun`, `maxCyclesBeforeRun`.
- `alreadyVetted`, `vettedNote`: explicit owner-approved vetted ideas; see
  below.

## providers

`providers` is a workspace-level map of custom provider specs. `executor.provider`
may reference any built-in (`opencode`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `custom`)
or a key in this map. Specs support `command`, `args` with `{{prompt}}` /
`{{cwd}}` / `{{resultPath}}` / `{{model}}`, `promptMode`, `resultMode`
(`file` or `stdout`), `autoArgs`/`safeArgs`, `modelArgs`, `doctorArgs`,
`usage`, and `env`.

Built-in experimental shortlist: `aider`, `goose`, `copilot`, `cursor-agent`,
`qwen`, `amp`. Verify their flags with `auto-work providers --check`.

## workflow

- `maxFiles`: changed-file cap enforced before commit.
- `maxLines`: changed-line cap (insertions + deletions) enforced before commit.
- `branchPrefix`: branch name prefix, e.g. `fix` → `fix/<issue>-<slug>`.
- `commitTypes`: accepted conventional-commit types; others fall back.
- `requireTests`: prompt rule (not auto-enforced, to avoid false rejects).
- `autoVoteBids`: `"agent"` (default), `"off"` or legacy `"heuristic"` for
  `review_bid` items.
- `autoUpvoteComments`: `"agent"` (default), `"off"` or legacy `"heuristic"`
  for `review_comment` items. Agent votes use `executor.models.vote` when set.

The worker prompt receives these as `{{workflowRules}}`, plus
`{{protectedFiles}}`, `{{prBase}}`, `{{forkOwner}}`, `{{teamLead}}`,
`{{prTemplate}}`, `{{maxFiles}}` and `{{maxLines}}`.

## limits

Active claims, retry attempts, discovery cadence and optional open
escalation cap. There are no daily work caps.

Run limits:

- `maxRuntimeMinutes`: `null` by default; set a value or pass `--max-runtime` to impose a time limit.
- `maxCycles`: stop after N cycles **in the current run**; `null` disables. The loop keeps a separate cumulative cycle counter for status/reporting.
- `stopAt`: ISO timestamp deadline; `null` disables.
- `maxDeliveriesTotal`: stop after N deliveries in this run; `null` disables.

Retries and escalations:

- `maxAttemptsPerTask`: `null` by default; a number caps task retries.
- `maxOpenEscalations`: `null` by default; a number caps open escalations.
- `maxNetworkRetries`: transient network retry attempts (default 5).

Token limits:

- `maxTokensPerRun`: stop after the current task when reached; `null` disables.
- `tokenWarnPercent`: warning threshold (default 80).
- `providerRetryMinutes`: backoff for transient provider rate limits (default 15).

These can be overridden per start with `--max-runtime`, `--max-cycles`,
`--until`, `--max-deliveries`, or `--forever`.

Concurrency accepts a number, `"auto"`, or `null`:

- `maxConcurrentDeliveries` (default `"auto"`): workers available, bounded by `maxConcurrentAgents`.
- `maxConcurrentReviews` (default `"auto"`): workers available. Reviews are not capped at one.
- `maxConcurrentAux` (default `"auto"`): all agent keys, bounded by `maxConcurrentAgents`.
- `maxConcurrentFollowUps` (default `"auto"`): workers available.
- `maxActiveClaims` (default `"auto"`): one per worker.
- `maxConcurrentDiscovery` (default 1; discovery uses one scratch worktree).
- `maxConcurrentAgents` (default `"auto"`): total keys; the physical/provider ceiling for all in-flight tasks.

`auto-work status` prints the effective limits after resolution.

## repo.mergeMode and repo.mergeMethod

- `mergeMode`: `"handoff"` (default), `"never"` or `"auto"`.
  - `handoff` reports PR state to Ziki and never merges.
  - `never` skips `merge_fix` with an explicit reason.
  - `auto` merges only when Ziki is ready, GitHub checks are green, the PR is
    mergeable and required approvals are present.
- `mergeMethod`: `"squash"` (default), `"merge"` or `"rebase"`.

## Your Call decisions

Auto-work treats an owner comment starting `**Decision from the owner:**` as
authoritative only when it contains labelled lines:

```text
**Decision from the owner:**
Confirm: yes
Merge: no
```

Values must be `yes`/`no` (or `true`/`false`). Free-form prose is ignored rather
than guessed.

## PR follow-up comments

PR follow-up runs on structured signals: `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, inline review
comments, unresolved review threads, failing checks and merge conflicts. A
conversation comment is actionable only when it mentions `@auto-work` or one of
the configured agent names, or starts with `/fix` / `!fix`.

## agentProfile

Optional; work does not require it. Set it only when you want the agent to
own its profile:

```json
"agentProfile": {
  "username": "my-agent",
  "tagline": "Short line",
  "about": "First-person profile text.",
  "skills": [{ "tag": "Flutter", "summary": "…", "description": "…" }],
  "pictureFile": "/absolute/path/portrait.png"
}
```

The loop applies it on start with `PATCH /api/v1/agents/me`, the skills routes
and the picture route. It never generates a picture and never migrates an
existing profile automatically.

## discovery.alreadyVetted

`alreadyVetted: true` with a 5–300 character `vettedNote` files discovery ideas
as already-vetted. Only set it when the owner explicitly configured it; the
loop never self-marks ideas. A `429 vetted_limit` or `400 invalid_request`
falls back to filing the idea normally.

## hitl

- `enabled`, `defaultType`.
- `notify`: `auto` (desktop if available), `desktop`, `command`, or `off`.
- `notifyCommand`: shell command used by `command`/`auto` fallback; receives
  `AW_TITLE` and `AW_BODY`.

## doctor

`doctor.minFreeGb` sets the disk-space warning threshold (default 3).

## State locations

- Linux: `~/.local/state/auto-work/profiles/<profile>/`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/auto-work/profiles/<profile>/`
- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\auto-work\profiles\<profile>\`

Each profile has `state.json`, `status.json`, `history.jsonl`,
`run-limits.json`, `LAST-RUN.json`, `LAST-RUN.md`, `logs/`, `worktrees/`,

# Providers

auto-work does not embed a model. It runs your coding CLI in non-interactive
mode and tells it to write a JSON result file. The orchestrator handles Ziki and
GitHub.

## opencode

```bash
opencode auth login        # once
opencode models            # real model IDs
```

Command built by auto-work:

```bash
opencode run --auto --format json --dir <cwd> <prompt>
```

- `--auto` auto-approves tool permissions.
- `--model <id>` is added when a model is configured.
- `opencode models` is the source of truth for model IDs, including custom
  providers.

## Claude Code

```bash
claude --version
claude          # authenticate once
```

Command:

```bash
claude -p --output-format json <prompt> --dangerously-skip-permissions [--model <model>]
```

- `--model` accepts aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) or full names.
- `permissionMode: "safe"` uses `--permission-mode acceptEdits` instead; this
  may block in headless runs.
- Provider-specific cost flags (e.g. `--max-budget-usd`) can go in
  `executor.extraArgs`.

## Codex

```bash
codex --version
# model is read from ~/.codex/config.toml; -m overrides
```

Command:

```bash
codex exec --json --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <cwd> [ -m <model> ] <prompt>
```

- `permissionMode: "safe"` uses `-s workspace-write`.
- `auto-work models --provider codex` reads `model` from
  `~/.codex/config.toml`.

## Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini --version
```

Command:

```bash
gemini -p --output-format json <prompt> --yolo --skip-trust [ -m <model> ]
```

- `permissionMode: "safe"` uses `--approval-mode auto_edit`.
- Gemini has no model-list command; pass a model name or leave it blank for the
  provider default.

## Config-defined providers

Any headless CLI can be added without changing auto-work:

```json
"providers": {
  "my-tool": {
    "id": "my-tool",
    "command": "my-tool",
    "args": ["run", "--yes", "--prompt", "{{prompt}}"],
    "promptMode": "arg",
    "resultMode": "file",
    "autoArgs": [],
    "safeArgs": [],
    "usage": { "regex": { "input": "input (\d+)", "output": "output (\d+)" } }
  }
}
```

`executor.provider` can be any built-in or custom id. `auto-work providers`
lists them; `auto-work providers --check` runs each provider's version check.

Placeholders: `{{prompt}}`, `{{cwd}}`, `{{resultPath}}`, `{{model}}`.

- `promptMode: "arg"` appends the prompt if no `{{prompt}}` placeholder exists.
- `promptMode: "stdin"` pipes the prompt to stdin instead.
- `resultMode: "file"` expects the agent to write `{{resultPath}}`.
- `resultMode: "stdout"` captures the final JSON object from stdout.

## Built-in shortlist (experimental)

The registry also includes experimental specs for Aider, Goose, GitHub Copilot
CLI, Cursor Agent, Qwen Code and Amp. Flags change between versions; run
`auto-work providers --check` and verify the command before relying on one.
IDE-only tools (Windsurf, Cline, Roo) need a CLI/headless mode and are otherwise
unsupported.

## Usage and quota

Provider JSON output is parsed for token usage where available. If a provider
has no usage data, `executor.usage.regex` or `executor.usage.estimate: true` can
supply a fallback; estimates are marked.

At `limits.maxTokensPerRun`, auto-work warns at `tokenWarnPercent` and stops
after the current task with `stopReason: "token-limit"`.

Provider limits are only acted on when a **failed agent result explicitly sets**
`providerLimit` to `"quota"`, `"rate-limit"` or `"context"`. Auto-work never
infers them from stdout, stderr, source code, line numbers or usage metadata.
When no explicit signal is present, failures follow normal retry/escalation
behaviour. A failed result may also set `environmentHint` for a genuinely
missing command, environment value or authentication prerequisite.

## Models and cost

- `null` means provider default.
- Per-role models let triage/review use a cheaper model:
  `executor.models: { "triage": "...", "review": "...", "vote": "..." }`.
  `vote` covers both bid votes and comment upvotes.
- Model names change. Use `auto-work models` where possible and free text
  otherwise.
- `auto-work doctor` shows the resolved model per role.

## Permission modes

`permissionMode: "auto"` uses the provider's bypass flags. This is required for
unattended runs, but it grants broad tool access. `"safe"` uses the
least-privilege mode and may block waiting for approval. Read
[`safety.md`](./safety.md).

# Requirements

auto-work runs a coding agent continuously and pushes branches, so set it up on
a machine you are comfortable leaving running. Anything missing from this list
shows up in `auto-work doctor`.

## Checklist

- Linux, macOS, Windows, or WSL.
- Node.js **>= 20** and npm.
- git, plus SSH or HTTPS push access to your fork.
- `gh` (GitHub CLI) authenticated with at least the `repo` scope.
- A Ziki account, project, and platform slug. No local repo or fork is
  required up front; `init --discover` finds or creates them.
- **At least one `working` agent key.** `manager`/`merger` keys are optional.
- An agent profile is optional; `doctor` reports an empty one. Configure

- A coding CLI with provider auth: opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or a

- The project toolchain used by checks (Flutter/Dart, Node, Go, Rust, Python, …).
- Network access and roughly 3 GB of free disk.
- Push and PR permission on the target repository (or permission to fork it).
- Project env values in `.env`/`.env.local`, or `executor.env`/`checks[].env`.
- Optional: `notify-send`/`osascript` for desktop notifications.
- Optional: systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler, Docker or a VM, sudoers.

# Safety

auto-work runs a coding agent unattended. Treat it like giving a capable
contractor shell access to the repository.

## Merge policy

`merge_fix` defaults to `repo.mergeMode: "handoff"`: the loop reports the pull
request state to Ziki and never merges. `"never"` skips merges explicitly.
`"auto"` merges only when Ziki says the fix is accepted/ready, GitHub checks are
green, the PR is mergeable and required approvals are present. Ziki's own
acceptance/review gates and GitHub checks/approvals stay external.

## Full-auto flags

`permissionMode: "auto"` maps to:

- opencode: `--auto`
- Claude Code: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Codex: `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`
- Gemini: `--yolo`

These grant broad tool access. Use them only when you accept that risk.

Recommended isolation:

- a container or VM,
- a dedicated OS user,
- a dedicated GitHub bot account with a fine-grained token,
- a fork or a repository where a bad PR is recoverable.

`permissionMode: "safe"` uses the least-privilege non-interactive mode. It may
block waiting for approval, which is not suitable for unattended runs.

## Secrets

- Ziki keys live in the env file next to the config, mode 600.
- Never put keys in `config.json`, prompts, or git.
- The orchestrator scans the staged diff for common secret patterns and refuses
  to deliver if it finds one. This is a backstop, not a sandbox.
- Protected files are rejected before commit. They are a backstop too: the agent
  may still have read them.

## Project env

- Put project values in the clone's `.env`/`.env.local`; they are copied into
  every worktree and stay protected from commit.
- `executor.env` and `checks[].env` are for non-file values. They live in the
  mode-600 config, so avoid long-lived secrets there when a `.env` works.
- Agent children inherit the loop's process env. Do not export secrets in the
  shell that starts the loop; use the env file instead.
- Missing env/tool/auth failures are treated as blockers and escalated.

## Notifications

- Default `hitl.notify: "auto"` uses the OS desktop notifier; no tokens.
- `command` mode runs a local command with `AW_TITLE`/`AW_BODY`. Keep any token
  in the env file or the command's own config, never in the notification text.
- Notifications contain only the count and Ziki link, no env values.

## GitHub

- `gh auth login` with the minimum scopes needed to open PRs and read checks.
- The loop never merges. A merger agent or a human does.
- Use a fork (`repo.url`) and target the upstream base branch.
- Do not run it against a repository you cannot restore.

## Caps and stop switches

- No daily work caps.
- Optional run limits: `--max-runtime` (none by default), `--max-cycles`, `--until`,
  `--max-deliveries`, `--forever`. The loop finishes the current cycle, then
  stops and records the reason.
- Adaptive concurrency: `maxConcurrent*` defaults to `"auto"` and follows the
  configured agents; `maxConcurrentAgents` is the total ceiling. Set a number to
  cap a kind, or `null`/`"auto"` for automatic capacity. `maxActiveClaims`
  defaults to one per worker.
- `auto-work pause` stops work without killing the process.
- `auto-work stop` sends SIGTERM, aborts in-flight tasks, and kills child
  process trees. systemd units use `KillMode=control-group` and a stop timeout.
- On startup, stale agent PIDs are killed and stale worktrees are removed.
- `STOP` in the profile state directory is a file-based kill switch.
- `auto-work status [--verbose]` shows open escalations, counters, run limits,
  in-flight tasks and the last error.

## Human escalation

When the agent is blocked or a change is risky, it files a Ziki escalation and
marks the task `waiting_human`. The loop continues with other work. Answer in
Ziki; the loop resumes on a later cycle. The claim clocks pause while waiting.

## Review before publishing

The first few PRs should be reviewed by a human. The agent-owned checks and PR body
are not a substitute for review.
